title: Trajectory property within a phase
statement: Let $I$ index a family of machines with state sets $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$, and let a reduction rule optionally send a state in phase $i$ to a state in one of the phases. Fix a phase $p$, a contract $C$ for its machine, and a trajectory predicate $R$. Suppose the halted state is not in the exit set of $C$, every state outside that exit set is left unchanged by the reduction rule in phase $p$, and every state in the exit set is sent to a state in a phase different from $p$. If $R$ holds throughout the trajectories of $C$, then it holds throughout the trajectories of the phase-hosted contract for the configuration formed by replacing the starting configuration's state with the entry state of $C$, with the same head-position vector.
hypotheses_covered: The halted state is not in X
Every state outside X has no reduction in phase p
Every state in X is reduced to a state in a phase other than p
replaced:
Let $I$ be an index type, let each $i\in I$ have a state set $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and a
machine $M_i$, and let a phase-host machine use a reduction rule $\mathrm{red}$ to move
between these phase state sets. Fix a phase $p$, an entry state $s_0\in\mathrm{Ph}(p)$,
a set $X\subseteq\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Ph}(p))$, and a contract $C$ for $M_p$ with
exits in $X$. Assume that the halted state is not in $X$, that $\mathrm{red}(p,s)$ is
undefined whenever $\mathrm{some}(s)\notin X$, and that whenever $\mathrm{some}(s)\in
X$, the reduction rule returns a state in a phase other than $p$. If $C$ satisfies the
trajectory property $R$, then the contract obtained by hosting $C$ in phase $p$
satisfies the property that, throughout its run, $R$ holds for the configuration whose
state is replaced by $s_0$ and for the same work-head positions.
